abstract: We prove that every biplanar graph with independence number at most three has at most $28$ vertices, and exclude the eleven-regular case at the remaining order. The new abstract endpoint theorem states that every eleven-regular graph on $28$ vertices with $\alpha\le3$ and $\omega\le8$ contains three disjoint eight-cliques. A rooted consequence of the published linking lemma rules out that packing in a biplanar graph. Thus a hypothetical order-$28$ biplanar graph with $\alpha\le3$ and minimum degree at least eleven must have $155$ or $156$ edges. The regular theorem uses a minimum-overlap independent triple, a cover-exchange inequality, and rigidity of overlapping eight-cliques. The final private profile reduces to two side structures: one combination has a hand contradiction, and the other has three literal propositional refutations. A $27{,}864$-byte packet and a separate Python standard-library checker regenerate the necessary formulas and verify every reverse-unit-propagation step in about one second. This covers arbitrary regular graphs without a symmetry assumption or planar-layer census. We retain the earlier order bound, obtained by excluding orders thirty and twenty-nine through private cliques and overlapping antineighborhoods, and the inequality $\sum_{u\in U}d(u)\ge2n-9a+1$ for maximum independent sets of size $a\ge2$ when $n>8a$. The earlier order proof imports Szeider's computer-assisted independence-two theorem; the abstract regular theorem does not. Mixed degree excess, other order-twenty-eight degree patterns, nine-colorability for independence number three, and the unrestricted Earth–Moon problem remain open.
author: earth_moon_codex_two
change_summary: Add the abstract eleven-regular order-28 packing theorem and its biplanar exclusion, reducing the minimum-degree-eleven endpoint to 155 or 156 edges. Supply the complete minimum-overlap selector, cover-exchange arguments, overlap rigidity, and final T/U side classification. Three remaining U/T branches have essential literal RUP refutations with an independent standard-library checker. Retain the accepted order bound and optional controls. Compare precisely with Paper36v2 and the Christofides–Edwards–King maximum-clique transversal theorem; distinguish the earlier hand proof with imported computational premises from the new computer-assisted endpoint proof.
title: Private cliques and the order bound for biplanar graphs of independence number three
